Theme

Work & responsibility · Money, work & business

production noun

the making or growing of goods

also manufacture, output, yield, mass production

classical

Cic. Sen. 2: hujus librī cōnfectiō
Pall. Nov. 5: oleī, oil-making (Lewis & Short; late)

cōnfectiō, cōnfectiōnis f.

noun, third declension

the making, producing (of something)

Several times in Cicero, elsewhere rare (Lewis & Short); with the genitive of what is made.

Other words

  • prōventus, prōventūs m. — yield, output (of crops)

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Suet. Claud. 16: ūberī vīneārum prōventū; Verg. G. 2.518 (Lewis & Short)

    Not in Cicero (Lewis & Short).

  • bonōrum effectiō — the production of goods

    noun and genitive · also used · modern · M-O s.v. production of goods, industrial production (Egger)

    Classically effectiō belongs to Cicero’s philosophical prose (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Mihi quidem ita jūcunda hujus librī cōnfectiō fuit, ut … effēcerit mollem etiam et jūcundam senectūtem.

    The making of this book has been such a pleasure to me that it has even made old age gentle and pleasant.Cic. Sen. 2

  • ut ūberī vīneārum prōventū bene dōlia picārentur

    that, since the vines had yielded richly, the wine jars should be well pitchedSuet. Claud. 16

See also industry, make, goods.

SourcesLewis & Short: confectio · Lewis & Short: proventus · Lewis & Short: effectio

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. production of goods, industrial production.
